# Story 18 — Agent replies to a live chat in real time

## Prerequisites

- Story 17 (auto-assign an escalated chat) — **shipped**. `Conversation.status` transitions to `"with_agent"` and `Conversation.assignedAgent` is populated by `pickAndClaimAgentForConversation()` in `backend/src/services/assignment.service.ts`, followed by a `conversation:assigned` broadcast at `backend/src/sockets/chat.socket.ts:231`.
- Story 14 (start a live chat) — provides the `Conversation`, `Message`, `conversation:join`, and `conversation:message` plumbing this story reuses end-to-end.
- Story 15 (AI agent responds first) — every conversation begins in `status: "ai_handling"`, so the "full conversation, including prior AI messages" this story must render already exists as `Message` documents with `senderType: "ai"`.
- Coordinate with the Story 19 planner (close a live chat conversation): both stories touch the same agent-side chat surface being introduced here; the agent list/detail view built in this story must leave a place for the Story 19 "mark resolved" control to slot in without a rewrite.

---

## Story Goal

Give an authenticated agent (or admin) a minimal but real UI to (1) see the live chats currently assigned to them, (2) open one and read the full prior transcript including AI messages, and (3) send replies over the existing `conversation:message` socket path so the customer receives them instantly. Fix the admin-bypass gap in `isAuthorizedOnConversation` so any admin can view/reply to any conversation.

**Not in scope:** the "mark resolved" button (Story 19), the polished unified agent dashboard (Story 20), quick replies, canned responses, presence, typing indicators for the human side.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Widen `isAuthorizedOnConversation` to accept an admin bypass

**File:** `backend/src/sockets/chat.socket.ts`

Change the signature from `(userId, conversation)` to `(user, conversation)` where `user = { id: string; role: string }`. New body:

```ts
function isAuthorizedOnConversation(
  user: { id: string; role: string },
  conversation: { customer: unknown; assignedAgent: unknown }
): boolean {
  if (user.role === "admin") return true;
  return user.id === String(conversation.customer) || user.id === String(conversation.assignedAgent);
}
```

Update the two call sites (currently at **lines 90 and 116**) to pass `socket.data.user` instead of `socket.data.user.id`.

Do **not** touch the customer-only guard at **lines 199–202** in the `conversation:escalate` handler — that guard is intentionally stricter than `isAuthorizedOnConversation` per the code comment there. Same for the `conversation:close` guard.

### 2 — Re-derive `senderType` so agents and admins both persist as `"agent"`

**File:** `backend/src/sockets/chat.socket.ts`, around **line 128** (the current `senderType` line inside `conversation:message`).

Current logic: `socket.data.user.id === String(conversation.customer) ? "customer" : "agent"`.

Replace with role-aware logic so the enum value is correct even when an admin (whose id is neither `conversation.customer` nor `conversation.assignedAgent`) sends a message:

```ts
const senderType: "customer" | "agent" =
  socket.data.user.id === String(conversation.customer) ? "customer" : "agent";
```

The above is already correct once the authorization check widens (an admin will fall through to `"agent"`, which is the intended enum value per `backend/src/models/Message.ts:44`). **No change to `senderType` derivation is needed beyond confirming this** — but add an inline comment noting that admins also serialize as `"agent"` (a UI-side distinction is out of scope; Story 24 handles internal notes / team roles).

### 3 — Add `GET /api/v1/conversations/:id` for the agent to load the transcript

**File:** `backend/src/routes/conversation.routes.ts`

Add a new handler between the existing `POST /` and the closing comment at lines 32–36:

- Path: `GET /:id`.
- Middleware: `requireAuth`, then `requireRole("agent", "admin", "customer")`. The customer branch is included so the same endpoint powers the customer chat view later, but this story only needs it working for staff; enforce per-caller authorization inside the handler using the **same rule** as widened `isAuthorizedOnConversation` (admin → allow; else caller id must equal `conversation.customer` or `conversation.assignedAgent`). On failure, respond `403` with `{ error: "You do not have permission to view this conversation" }`.
- Response body: `{ conversation, messages }` where `messages = await Message.find({ parentType: "conversation", parentId: id }).sort({ createdAt: 1 }).lean();`. Cap at a reasonable page size (e.g. **500** most-recent, or none if pagination is easier to skip — no live chat should approach this). Do **not** filter by `senderType`; the AI transcript must be included per the acceptance criterion.
- Validate `:id` via `objectIdSchema` (already imported in `chat.socket.ts`; add the same import here from `../validation/common`).
- `404` when `Conversation.findById` returns null.

Also add a `GET /` staff-scoped list endpoint used by the new `/chats` page:

- Path: `GET /`.
- Middleware: `requireAuth`, `requireRole("agent", "admin")`.
- Agent branch: `Conversation.find({ assignedAgent: req.user.id, status: { $in: ["with_agent", "escalated"] } }).sort({ updatedAt: -1 }).lean();`.
- Admin branch (`req.user.role === "admin"`): same query but without the `assignedAgent` restriction (admins can see any active human-handled conversation).
- Response: `{ conversations }`.

**Do not** page these yet — a follow-up in the `platform/paginate-list-views` intake covers pagination consistently across list endpoints.

**File:** `backend/src/app.ts`. Grep for the existing `conversation.routes` mount (added by Story 14). No change needed unless the mount uses a stricter path — confirm it is `app.use("/api/v1/conversations", conversationRoutes)`.

The existing broadcast at **line 138** (`io.to(\`conversation:${conversationId}\`).emit("conversation:message", message)`) is already the exact real-time delivery path this story's acceptance criterion requires — the agent's message will land in the customer's `LiveChatPanel.tsx` handler at line 113 with zero frontend backend contract change on the customer side. Verify this by re-reading `LiveChatPanel.tsx:113` and confirming it renders every `senderType` value it receives.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Agent tries to open a chat that is not assigned to them, and is not an admin.** The new `GET /:id` handler returns `403`; the Next detail page falls back to `notFound()`. Enforced in the handler added in step 3 (see `backend/src/routes/conversation.routes.ts`).
- **Admin opens a chat they were never assigned to.** Widened `isAuthorizedOnConversation` (step 1) allows it on the socket path; the REST handler (step 3) mirrors the same rule. Add explicit tests for both paths.
- **Agent sends a message on a conversation still in `status: "ai_handling"`.** Should succeed — the current handler at `chat.socket.ts:123` only blocks `"resolved"`. Confirm and add a regression test so a future change does not accidentally re-gate this.
- **Customer somehow reaches `GET /:id` for another customer's conversation.** Handler must `403`. Do not `404` to avoid leaking existence — mirror the reasoning documented in `.squad/stories/ticket-management/view-and-filter-the-ticket-queue/intake.md:87`.
- **Socket disconnects mid-conversation on the agent side.** On reconnect, `AgentChatPanel` re-emits `conversation:join`; the server re-authorizes via the widened check. No local buffering of unsent text is required in this story; document as a follow-up TODO in the component.
- **Empty text / whitespace-only submissions.** Already rejected by `conversationMessagePayloadSchema` (see the existing test at `backend/tests/sockets/chat.socket.test.ts:160`). No frontend re-validation required beyond disabling the Send button when the trimmed input is empty.
- **`conversation.status === "resolved"`.** Already blocked at `chat.socket.ts:123` for messages; the new `GET /:id` still returns the conversation and its messages (read-only view) — the composer is disabled by the frontend rule in step 8. Story 19 will land the actual "close" control; this story must not silently prevent viewing resolved conversations.
- **Admin's own outgoing message is stored as `senderType: "agent"`.** Intentional (Message enum has no "admin"). Add an inline comment near step 2 explaining this so a future reader does not "fix" it.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `cd backend && npm run build`.
2. **Backend tests:** `cd backend && npm test -- chat.socket` and `npm test -- conversation.routes`.
3. **Frontend builds:** `cd frontend && npm run build`.
4. **End-to-end smoke (two browsers):**
   1. In browser A, sign in as a customer, start a live chat, exchange one or two messages with the AI, then send "talk to a human". Confirm `Conversation.status` flips to `"with_agent"` and `assignedAgent` is set (Story 17 already covers this).
   2. In browser B, sign in as the assigned agent, navigate to `/chats`, click into the same conversation, confirm the entire transcript (customer + AI messages) is visible.
   3. Type a reply in browser B and send. Confirm it appears in browser A **instantly** (no page refresh) via the existing `conversation:message` handler.
   4. Sign browser B out and back in as an `admin` who is NOT the assigned agent. Navigate to `/chats/<same id>` directly. Confirm read + reply both work (admin bypass).
5. **Regression:** re-run the Story 14/15/16/17 socket tests in `backend/tests/sockets/chat.socket.test.ts` to confirm none regressed.
